mission: Phase-5 training-coverage redesign & causal merchant history

integrity_fix.bug: _merchant_volume.npz was built by hashing str((name, year)) TUPLES instead of the merchant name - its 99,602 codes lived in a different hash space than every frame's merchant_id and were validated wrong (code 65721 = 228 rows in table vs 1.13M in file).
integrity_fix.fix: cs_merch_volume.py corrected to hash the merchant name; table rebuilt (63,288 codes x 30 years, 53s) and validated against awk ground truth and _merchant_table.npz (identical sorted code sets).
integrity_fix.impact: 5% pool coverage is 47.0% of active merchants (not 27.6%); 53.0% absent (not ~31%). Taxonomy re-derived: 12.2% of absent legit val rows genuinely new (not ~2%); D bucket 423->7 (misalignment artifact). CS novelty features (merch_prior_*) rebuilt on the corrected table. E_hardneg (48 self-derived native features) UNAFFECTED. Coverage-simulation model metrics UNAFFECTED (they were frame-derived, never used the volume table).

frame.sampling: all fraud + per-merchant legit cap 200 (L<=200 all kept, L>200 w.p. 200/L) keyed on full-corpus pre-2016 legit volume; TRAIN-ONLY; seed 42

label_latency.mission: PS-14 Phase-5 label-latency status: current unresolved label-availability evidence (unchanged from Phase 4 - no new evidence found)

dataset.label_creation: Assigned at generation time by the IBM synthetic generator (pre-labeled static file). No in-repo label-creation pipeline, investigation step, or confirmation timestamp exists.
dataset.label_availability_timestamp: ABSENT - no column or metadata records when a label would become available to a real-time scorer

count_only_establishment_features.merchant_age: label-free; birth year from full-corpus table; causal
count_only_establishment_features.merch_prior_rows: label-free; cumulative corpus rows in years < row year

label_dependent_fraud_rate_features.user_fraud_rate: uses fraud labels (ground-truth expanding cumsum in training)
label_dependent_fraud_rate_features.status: UNVERIFIED - require label-availability evidence before a deployable candidate may rely on them

training_definition.semantics: ground-truth expanding fraud counts over the sampled chronological stream (entity-level cumsum over prior rows)
training_definition.window: full history before the current row (expanding)

production_definition.semantics: rolling 100-event window per entity (user/merchant/city), min_events=5, baseline fallback 0.001
production_definition.label_source: PROXY - the risk engine's OWN decision (ml/score >= 70), NOT ground-truth fraud
production_definition.window: rolling 100 events (vs training expanding full history)
production_definition.note: These are different quantities even at zero label latency. The proxy labels are the model's own decisions (self-referential); confirmed-feedback labels would only enter through _record_entity_rates with is_fraud from a real investigation, which no caller currently provides.

label_latency.parity: DIVERGENT - window (100-event rolling vs expanding), label source (proxy decision vs ground truth), and update mechanism all differ
label_latency.minimum_required_label_delay: UNDEFINED - the static dataset cannot establish any confirmation delay; a production deployment would need to define it (e.g., confirmed-feedback events only)
label_latency.production_can_provide: Only if confirmed-feedback labels (analyst investigation outcomes) are fed to the tracker. The current score>=70 proxy must be replaced or the three fraud-rate features dropped from any deployable redesign candidate.
consequence_for_phase5: Ablations that keep user_fraud_rate/merch_fraud_rate/city_fraud_rate are development-only diagnostics.

Any deployable redesigned candidate must either (a) drop the 3 label-dependent fraud-rate features, (b) receive confirmed-feedback labels through the tracker, or (c) keep them with an explicit UNVERIFIED + self-referential-proxy qualification.
Label-free establishment/exposure features are the safe path and are prioritized.

decision_matrix.question: Labels available causally?
decision_matrix.finding: UNVERIFIED - static generator labels, no availability timestamp
decision_matrix.consequence: fraud-rate features stay UNVERIFIED; count-only features safe

decision_matrix.question: Corrected merchant coverage?
decision_matrix.consequence: coverage gap real but 5% pool is NOT as small as previously claimed

decision_matrix.question: Are 'unseen' merchants new?
decision_matrix.consequence: coverage redesign must help BOTH; new merchants stay ~76% flagged

decision_matrix.question: Does greater coverage reduce absent FPR?
decision_matrix.finding: YES on identical rows: 0.636 -> 0.552 (cov_20) / 0.588 (C) at P1
decision_matrix.consequence: coverage lever CONFIRMED as primary cause

decision_matrix.question: Does Strategy C dominate?
decision_matrix.finding: NO on fixed population - overall FPR 0.159 vs 0.067 control (count-scale confound)
decision_matrix.consequence: C proves coverage mechanism but needs exposure-normalized count features (#15-16) before deployment

decision_matrix.question: Establishment history helps?
decision_matrix.finding: 2-3 pts absent FPR at ~1 pt overall cost (phase-2/3); C includes full small-merchant coverage

decision_matrix.question: Is global threshold appropriate?
decision_matrix.finding: No - absent-code rows 74-86% flagged at all history depths
decision_matrix.consequence: conditional thresholding is an output of the redesign, not a fix

decision_matrix.question: Is another model justified now?
decision_matrix.finding: Not yet - count-scale control (#15) must land first
decision_matrix.consequence: OUTCOME B: keep E_hardneg; build exposure-normalized features next

verdict.finding: Coverage reduces absent-merchant FPR on identical rows (0.636 -> 0.552-0.588 at 10-20%/C) BUT naive coverage scaling moves the COUNT-feature distribution away from the 5%-scale evaluation population, so seen/overall FPR rises (0.059 -> 0.09-0.15). This is the sampling-scale confound mission #15 predicted: count/velocity features encode how many rows were SAMPLED, not merchant behavior. A deployment-safe redesign therefore requires exposure-normalized / rate-based count features (#15/#16) so a model trained at one scale scores rows at any scale identically.
verdict.outcome: OUTCOME A/B boundary - KEEP E_hardneg deployed. Strategy C PROVES the coverage lever (100% merchant coverage with 2.33M train rows) but does NOT yet dominate E_hardneg on the fixed population because count features are sampling-scale-sensitive. Next experiment (mission #15-16): exposure-aware normalization of the 20+ count/velocity features, then re-run the identical fixed-population protocol.
